title: Dokimasia disposition set
description: The reviewer's own artefact: one entry per scoped item a decision has been drafted or made for, written against the exact inventory and workbook digests it was built from. Every entry carries a `confirmed` boolean, and only a confirmed entry is admitted as a disposition; an unconfirmed one is a draft this tool wrote and nobody has agreed to. A confirmed entry names the person whose judgement admits it in `confirmed_by`, and may name a `rule` from the set-level `rules` table, where each rule's text and the person who stated it are written once. Closed, so an unknown key is a refusal. `propose` emits the set, which brings it under the rule that every emitted record is checked against its committed schema; it never writes either attribution field.

inventory_sha256.description: The inventory record this set was written against. A set naming a digest that has moved is stale and refuses rather than being carried forward.

workbook_sha256.description: The workbook record this set was written against, under the same staleness rule.

generated_by.description: The skill version that drafted this set, present when a generator wrote it and absent on a set written entirely by hand. It records provenance and confers no authority: a generated entry is still admitted only once a person confirms it.

rules.description: The rules confirmed entries may name, keyed by a rule id that is one safe path segment of at most 64 bytes. Optional: a set whose every confirmation was made individually declares none. A row nobody applies is reported as applied zero times, not refused. The reconciler bounds the table at 256 rows.

text.description: The rule as the person who stated it worded it, written once here rather than on every entry confirmed under it. Bound by the reason cap, and refused blank.

stated_by.description: The person who stated the rule. A claim the file makes under a person's name, not a verified identity; nothing here signs it.

item.description: The scoped item this entry decides, named as the reconciler names it.

disposition.description: ADR-001 fixes this set at three states. A generator may write only `manual` or `excluded`; `covered` is reserved to a person holding an item to a reviewed oracle, and no proposal path constructs it.

reason.description: Why a `manual` or `excluded` item was decided that way. Optional here and required there: the reconciler reads an absent reason as the empty string and then refuses those two states for carrying none, which is a stronger check than presence, because it also catches a reason that is present and blank. An unexplained exclusion is how a denominator shrinks quietly.

oracle.description: The workbook case a covered item is held to. Optional here for the same reason, and refused by the reconciler on any disposition other than `covered`, because an entry reading as both decided-by-a-person and held-to-a-case states two different things about one item.

confirmed.description: A person's mark, and the only thing that admits this entry as a disposition. False on every entry a generator writes, and a generator cannot set it true. An unconfirmed entry leaves its item undisposed and holds the closure ratio down exactly as an absent entry does.

proposed_sha256.description: The digest of the entry as it was drafted, recorded so a regeneration can tell an untouched draft from one a person edited. Absent on an entry written by hand, which is never treated as untouched.

confirmed_by.description: The person whose judgement admits this entry. Required by the reconciler on every confirmed entry and refused on an unconfirmed one; optional here only because the schema cannot state that conditional. Absent, blank or non-string on a confirmed entry refuses by name rather than defaulting, because defaulting a person is the forgery attribution exists to prevent. No generator writes it.

rule.description: The id of the row in `rules` this entry was confirmed under, when a person applied a stated rule rather than deciding the entry individually. An id the table does not hold refuses. Refused on an unconfirmed entry. No generator writes it.
